original_question: Construct a system of scalar invariants of a projective structure that vanish if and only if there exists (locally, in a neighborhood of almost every point) a metric compatible with a given projective structure.
target_in_paper: Problem 12.0.5 in Section 12, How to reconstruct a metric from its geodesics; this draft is essentially the paper’s own formulation, so it does not target Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem almost verbatim: it asks for scalar invariants of a projective structure, requires an if-and-only-if criterion, and phrases the criterion as local existence of a compatible metric near almost every point. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient object should be stated explicitly: a smooth projective structure [∇] on a smooth manifold M, arising from unparameterized geodesics. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

For the question to be stand-alone, 'projective structure' should be defined as an equivalence class of torsion-free affine connections having the same unparameterized geodesics; equivalently, representatives satisfy Γ̄^i_{jk}=Γ^i_{jk}+δ^i_k φ_j+δ^i_j φ_k. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The intended meaning of 'metric compatible with a given projective structure' should be made explicit: a nondegenerate Riemannian or semi-Riemannian metric g whose Levi-Civita connection belongs to the projective class [∇]. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The locality quantifier should be written pointwise: for almost every p∈M there exists a neighborhood U of p on which such a metric exists. The paper itself leaves 'almost every point' informal, so it should be preserved rather than silently strengthened to every point. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The paper does not impose finiteness of the invariant system, an a priori bound on differential order, or an algorithmic/computational requirement, so those restrictions should not be added in the refinement. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The nearby context notes that the 2-dimensional case is already solved in Bryant–Dunajski–Eastwood, so the genuinely open part is the higher-dimensional case. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))

The invariants are meant to be projective scalar differential invariants, i.e. quantities depending only on the projective class rather than on a chosen representative connection. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a smooth manifold and [∇] a smooth projective structure on M, meaning an equivalence class of torsion-free affine connections with the same unparameterized geodesics (equivalently, Γ̄^i_{jk}=Γ^i_{jk}+δ^i_k φ_j+δ^i_j φ_k). Construct scalar projective differential invariants of [∇] whose simultaneous vanishing is equivalent to local metrizability in the following sense: for almost every point p∈M, there exists a neighborhood U of p and a nondegenerate Riemannian or semi-Riemannian metric g on U whose Levi-Civita connection belongs to [∇]|_U. The two-dimensional case is already known, so the unresolved content is in higher dimensions. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
justification: This is exactly Problem 12.0.5. The surrounding discussion in Section 12 first defines path structures, then explains projective equivalence of torsion-free affine connections via equation (12.3), and then states that reconstructing a metric from unparameterized geodesics amounts to the local existence of a compatible metric for the resulting projective structure. Immediately before the problem, the paper also records the theoretical reformulation in terms of nondegenerate parallel sections of a certain tensor bundle, and immediately after it notes that dimension 2 is already solved and points to higher-dimensional obstruction work. ([users.fmi.uni-jena.de](https://users.fmi.uni-jena.de/~matveev/Datei/problem_list_submitted.pdf))
